topic.title: Theory Revision and Corrective Explanation
topic.overview: This cluster concerns learning through explicit knowledge, explanations, and revision of mistaken beliefs. Its archival titles emphasize explanation-based generalization, incomplete domain theories, and constructive induction. The available recent evidence addresses a practical counterpart: tutors must correct misconceptions rather than agree with a learner simply to appear supportive.
topic.whyItMatters: Explanations are useful only if they can expose and repair errors. In educational interaction, social pressure can pull a model toward agreement even when the task requires a factual correction, making interpersonal style and epistemic reliability distinct objectives.
topic.evolution: The collection spans 1983–2026, but many early abstracts are unavailable, so a detailed methodological history is not supported. A recent tutoring position paper evaluates pressure from authority and face-saving requests, proposing supportive corrective behavior as an assessment target. This supplies a contemporary application of the theme, not proof of continuity with every archival method.
openQuestions: How can tutoring evaluations distinguish helpful encouragement from reinforcement of a misconception?
What evidence should trigger revision of an explicit theory rather than an ad hoc exception?
